The excerpts I found don't have a full side-by-side comparison, and they say little about the Get Clássica's features. Here is what they do cover.

**Monthly cost if you don't reach the sales threshold (rental plan)**
- Get Clássica: R$ 79.90/month
- Get Smart: R$ 129.90/month

**Sales needed for a free machine**
- At R$ 10k/month in sales, you can get the Get Mini or the Get Clássica free.
- At R$ 60k/month, the Get Smart is also available.

**Get Smart features**
- It is exclusive to CNPJ (company) accounts with revenue above R$10k/month.
- It has an app store with more than 150 solutions, such as cashback, giftback and inventory control.
- It prints receipts, has a barcode reader and integrated management software.
- It can be used as a TEF solution, integrated with your cash register automation.
- It supports payment splitting.

You need an account to receive Pix sales, but it doesn't have to be a traditional bank account. It also doesn't have to be a Getnet account.

- **Pix key:** To sign up for Pix at Getnet, you give one Pix key that is linked to the account where you want to receive the money.
- **Existing bank account:** One Getnet FAQ page lists these requirements: a compatible capture method (terminal, TEF or e-commerce), a Santander bank domicile with an active Pix key, and registration with an individual (PF) legal representative. Another page says you can sign up using the same key you registered with your bank. It adds that availability depends on which payment service providers (PSPs) are already integrated with Getnet, so check with customer service.
- **No bank account:** Get Conta is a free digital account for your business. You can send and receive money and sell through Pix with it. You can also open one without a card machine through digital onboarding ("Credenciamento" > "Sem máquina").

To confirm which accounts work for your business, contact customer service at 4002 4000 or 0800 648 8000, or use the Getnet app.

Your Get Smart machine (GS-1988-0001) has had no Wi-Fi signal for "PaoDourado" since its last restart. Its 4G chip is active, so 4G is available as a backup. I couldn't find a step-by-step guide for Wi-Fi problems in Getnet's official content, so the steps below are general suggestions rather than official policy.

- **Check the router.** Make sure the "PaoDourado" router is on and the internet is working, for example by testing another device. Keep the machine close to the router.
- **Switch to 4G.** Use the active chip as your connection while Wi-Fi is down.
- **Run a communication test.** Getnet's FAQ describes this test for chip connectivity. Press the function button (F, # or the one on your machine), then 60, then option 2 (maintenance), then option 1 (communication test). The FAQ is written for other machine models, so the menu may differ on your Get Smart.
- **Restart the machine.** Do this after the steps above.

If it's still offline after these steps, I can open a ticket for you. You can also contact Getnet through the app or customer service.

Here is what Getnet's official content says about receivables advance (antecipação de vendas):

- **When you can advance:** A sale becomes available for advance from D+1 (one business day after the sale) until D-3 (three business days before the amount would be credited to your account). For example, a sale made on 04/03 can be advanced from 05/03. If the credit date is 03/04, it can be advanced until 31/03.
- **How to request it:** the options are the same for Santander account holders and non-holders:
  - Automatic advance
  - One-off advance through Getnet's Customer Service
  - Advance on the POS, done by the merchant on the Getnet terminal
- **Extra options for Santander account holders:** through your branch manager, or through Internet Banking (including the business channel, if it is enabled).
- **Checking it:** The day after the advance, you can see the advanced Mastercard/Visa sales in the Santander Portal under Consultas > Extratos por período > Antecipação por período.
- **Automatic advance and fees:** Automatic advance is a condition for the exemption on the "Receba Conforme suas Vendas" plan. Getnet assesses each contract individually, as it involves credit approval. The standard sales rates don't include the advance fee, if you contract it.

There isn't a fixed number of installments for the crediário. Each card issuer sets the installment limit according to its own credit policies.

To see the options and interest for a specific sale:
- On the card machine, insert the card, enter the amount and choose credit > crediário. The machine will show a simulation.
- You can print the simulation if the machine has paper, so your customer can see the interest and the final purchase amount.
- The simulation is for reference only and is subject to credit analysis. The card issuer decides whether to approve the transaction.

For you as the merchant, the number of installments doesn't change when you get paid. Crediário sales are paid in a single payment, within 2 business days after the transaction is captured, however many installments the cardholder chooses.

Yes. Getnet's Payment Link (Get Link & Pay) is meant for selling through WhatsApp, SMS or your preferred social network.

- **Sharing:** You can make sales using WhatsApp, SMS or your preferred social network.
- **Customization:** The link can be customized with product details.
- **Security:** The link includes anti-fraud security.
- **Payment methods:** The Brazilian Payment Link page says it accepts debit, credit, Pix, Wallet and boleto. The English page only mentions debit and credit.

**Before you start:**
- Even if you already use Getnet in-store, you must pass the risk and prevention reviews before online sales are enabled.
- If you go more than 4 months without any transactions, the Payment Link is disabled and you have to go through all the approvals again.
